The '''1940 Masters Tournament''' was the seventh [[Masters Tournament]], held April{{nbsp}}4–7 at [[Augusta National Golf Club]] in [[Augusta, Georgia]].

[[Jimmy Demaret]] won the first of his three Masters titles, four strokes ahead of runner-up [[Lloyd Mangrum]],<ref name=cdtdemwn>{{cite news |url=http://archives.chicagotribune.com/1940/04/08/page/21/article/demarets-280-wins-masters-mangrum-2d |newspaper=Chicago Daily Tribune |last=Bartlett |first=Charles |title=Demaret's 280 wins Masters; Mangrum 2d |date=April 8, 1940 |page=21}}</ref><ref name=jdcmt>{{cite news|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=zhNKAAAAIBAJ&sjid=oYUMAAAAIBAJ&pg=4008%2C2454862 |newspaper=Youngstown Vindicator|location=Ohio|agency=United Press|last=Ferguson|first=Harry|title=Jimmy Demaret captures Masters Tournament|date=April 8, 1940|page=10}}</ref> the largest margin of victory until [[1948 Masters Tournament|1948]]. The purse was $5,000 and the winner's share was $1,500.

Mangrum shot an opening round 64{{nbsp}}(−8), a new course record by two strokes,<ref name=lm64lao>{{cite news|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=205QAAAAIBAJ&sjid=CQ0EAAAAIBAJ&pg=5697%2C659716|newspaper=Milwaukee Sentinel|title=Lloyd Mangrum's 64 leads Augusta Open|agency=Associated Press|date=April 5, 1940|page=21}}</ref><ref name=cdtcbtlt>{{cite news |url=http://archives.chicagotribune.com/1940/04/05/page/33/article/mangrum-leads-masters-golf-on-record-64 |newspaper=Chicago Daily Tribune |last=Bartlett |first=Charles |title=Mangrum leads Masters golf on record 64 |date=April 5, 1940 |page=33}}</ref><ref name=cfire>{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=mG5WAAAAIBAJ&sjid=9OMDAAAAIBAJ&pg=6868%2C1212486 |newspaper=Spokesman-Review |location=Spokane, Washington |agency=Associated Press |title=Lloyd Mangrum catches fire to set competitive golf scoring record |date=April 5, 1940 |page=14}}</ref><ref name=ppcind >{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=KeUdAAAAIBAJ&sjid=VkwEAAAAIBAJ&pg=3818%2C403720 |newspaper=Pittsburgh Press |agency=United Press |last=Ferguson |first=Harry |title=Golf's Mr. Cinderella paces Masters play |date=April 5, 1940 |page=44}}</ref> and it stood for 46{{nbsp}}years, until [[Nick Price]]'s{{nbsp}}63 in [[1986 Masters Tournament|1986]],<ref name=nlbphst>{{cite news|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=g1dOAAAAIBAJ&sjid=IRQEAAAAIBAJ&pg=6432,3566749|newspaper=Sunday Star News|agency=Associated Press|title=Norman leads but Price has 63|location=Wilmington, North Carolina|date=April 13, 1986|page=1B}}</ref> later equaled by [[Greg Norman]] in [[1996 Masters Tournament|1996]]. Although all three of these players won [[Men's major golf championships|major]] titles, none won a Masters.

==Field==
;1. Masters champions
[[Ralph Guldahl]] (2,9,10), [[Byron Nelson]] (2,9,10,12), [[Henry Picard]] (6,9,10,12), [[Gene Sarazen]] (2,4,6,9), [[Horton Smith]] (9,10,12)

;2. [[U.S. Open (golf)|U.S. Open]] champions
[[Tommy Armour]] (4,6,9,10), [[Billy Burke (golfer)|Billy Burke]] (9), [[Chick Evans]] (3,a), [[Johnny Farrell]], [[Walter Hagen]] (4,6), [[Bobby Jones (golfer)|Bobby Jones]] (3,4,5), [[Tony Manero (golfer)|Tony Manero]] (9), [[George Sargent (golfer)|George Sargent]]

;3. [[U.S. Amateur]] champions
[[Lawson Little]] (5,9)

;4. [[The Open Championship|British Open]] champions

;5. [[The Amateur Championship|British Amateur]] champions
[[Charlie Yates]] (8,9,a)

;6. [[PGA Championship|PGA]] champions
[[Johnny Revolta]] (10), [[Paul Runyan]] (9,10,12)

;7. Members of the U.S. [[Ryder Cup]] team
*''Not held''

;8. Members of the U.S. [[1938 Walker Cup]] team
[[Ray Billows]] (11,a), [[Chuck Kocsis]] (a), [[Tommy Suffern Tailer]] (9,a), [[Bud Ward]] (10,11,a)

*''[[Johnny Fischer]] (3,a), [[Johnny Goodman]] (2,3,5,a), [[Fred Haas]] (a) and [[Reynolds Smith]] (a) did not play. Tailer was a reserve for the team.''

;9. Top 30 players and ties from the [[1939 Masters Tournament]]
[[Ed Dudley]] (10), [[Vic Ghezzi]] (10), [[Chick Harbert]] (a), [[Jimmy Hines]] (10), [[Ben Hogan]], [[Ky Laffoon]] (10), [[Jug McSpaden]] (10), [[Frank Moore (golfer)|Frank Moore]], [[Toney Penna]], [[Felix Serafin]] (10), [[Sam Snead]] (10), [[Jimmy Thomson (golfer)|Jimmy Thomson]], [[Willie Turnesa]] (a), [[Frank Walsh (golfer)|Frank Walsh]], [[Al Watrous]], [[Craig Wood (golfer)|Craig Wood]] (10)

*''[[Denny Shute]] (4,6,10) and [[Jess Sweetser]] (3,5,a) did not play.''

;10. Top 30 players and ties from the [[1939 U.S. Open (golf)|1939 U.S. Open]]
[[Johnny Bulla]], [[Sammy Byrd]], [[Harry Cooper (golfer)|Harry Cooper]], [[Bobby Cruickshank]], [[Jimmy Demaret]], [[Jim Foulis]], [[Dutch Harrison]] (12), [[Clayton Heafner]], [[Dick Metz]] (12), [[Ed Oliver (golfer)|Ed Oliver]], [[Wilford Wehrle]] (a)

*''[[Olin Dutra]] (2,6), [[Matt Kowal]] and [[John Rogers (golfer)|John Rogers]] did not play.''

;11. 1939 [[U.S. Amateur]] quarter-finalists
[[George Dawson (golfer)|George Dawson]] (a), [[Art Doering]] (a)

*''[[Harry Givan]] (a), [[Ed Kingsley]] (a) and [[Don Schumacher (golfer)|Don Schumacher]] (a) did not play.''

;12. [[1939 PGA Championship]] quarter-finalists
[[Rod Munday]]

*''[[Emerick Kocsis]] did not play.''

;13. One amateur, not already qualified, selected by a ballot of ex-U.S. Amateur champions
[[Bill Holt]] (a)

;14. One professional, not already qualified, selected by a ballot of ex-U.S. Open champions
*''[[Macdonald Smith]] did not play.''

;15. Two players, not already qualified, with the best scoring average in the winter part of the 1940 PGA Tour
[[Willie Goggin]], [[Lloyd Mangrum]]

;16 Foreign invitations
[[Enrique Bertolino]], [[Jim Ferrier]] (a), [[Jules Huot]], [[Martin Pose]], [[Robert Sweeny Jr.]] (a)
